newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian refugees continue exodus to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albanian refugees continue exodus to Italy.

text.p: More than 1,300 Albanian refugees sailed to southern Italy overnight in a flotilla of ramshackle boats, as the exodus from the troubled Balkan state continued unabated.
Port authorities said 629 Albanians reached Bari early on Tuesday aboard three fishing boats.
A short distance down the coast, 487 people arrived in Brindisi on a single boat which limped into harbour with engine problems. Another 214 people came in on two trawlers.

The number of Albanians who have fled to Italy over the last six days to escape armed chaos in their homeland is more than 7,500. Coast guards said on Tuesday that their radars showed more Albanian boats were heading towards the Italian coast.
The army of refugees have been lodged in makeshift reception centres and hundreds have been moved to other regions to ease the pressure on crowded facilities in south eastern Italy.

Italy, which was hit by an exodus of tens of thousands of Albanians in 1991 after communist rule crumbled, has said it will grant refugees only temporary sanctuary and has appealed to other Albanians not to try to follow them.
